correctness.summary: The standard bound retains the actual auxiliary rank surplus in Zhu's range comparison. A branching vertex creates a triangle surplus, even cycles admit an exact conditioned-increment surplus formula, and an elementary integral bound converts both to an explicit n^{-1/2} gap. A fork tree gives the matching order by an exact reflection-principle identity. The lazy cyclic bound follows from Zhu's explicit p=2/3 margin, while the tree bound transfers standard stability through zero-edge contraction. Algebraic identities and constants were checked by a standalone script.

limitations: The constants are convenient rather than optimized.
The universal lazy n^{-3/2} exponent is not shown sharp.
The proof uses specific comparison and rank-surplus lemmas from Zhu (2026) as prior inputs.
Only expected range is treated, not full stochastic domination.
The full Wu--Xu--Zhu (2016) text was not inspected; tree-specific originality therefore retains a material residual risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Path extremality, tree and unicyclic special cases, lazy tree stochastic domination, and Zhu's auxiliary comparison machinery are prior art. The sources inspected did not state the dimension-explicit universal stability gaps or the sharp n^{-1/2} standard stability order exhibited here. The strongest residual risk is the 2016 Wu--Xu--Zhu tree paper, whose full text could not be inspected and may contain a quantitative tree refinement under different notation.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result identifies a sharp stability scale behind the newly solved expected-range extremal problem, supplies a near-extremal family, and quantifies uniqueness in both standard and lazy models.
